pill.desc: white to light yellow, oval tablet

clues.kinetics: Oral bioavailability is only about 0.4% to 1% at 3 to 14 mg, and higher with 50 mL of water than with 240 mL. It is over 99% bound to albumin and is mainly eliminated by metabolism of the peptide backbone.
clues.substance: Its backbone is made by yeast fermentation; it is a hygroscopic powder with a molecular weight of 4113.58.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as tablets from 1.5 mg to 14 mg, taken once daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents. Contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, and after serious hypersensitivity such as anaphylaxis or angioedema.
clues.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, and reducing major cardiovascular events in those at high risk.
clues.mechanism: Selectively activates the GLP-1 receptor, stimulating insulin secretion and lowering glucagon in a glucose-dependent way. It also causes a minor delay in gastric emptying.

tell: A co-formulated SNAC absorption enhancer and a roughly one-week half-life set this oral GLP-1 receptor agonist apart.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Semaglutide maximum concentration was reached approximately 1-hour after oral administration
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: Semaglutide elimination half-life is approximately one week
